html:
SMTO-LLM-0089 — The model service couldn't find that model name

GUID: 2b8c1b8f-95d0-46e0-acf7-b0f788f997e2
Slug: provider-model-not-found
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: readiness

What happened

  • The model service doesn't recognize the model name SMTO sent, so it couldn't answer. The name may be misspelled, or the model may have been removed, renamed or not shared with this account.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing, open the Main card, turn off Auto-select model if it's on, and select Discover models to see the names the service offers. Choosing from the list avoids typing mistakes in the model name.
  2. Choose the correct model, or type the exact name the service's manager gives you. Select Save Main, then select Check saved model, and start a new task. New tasks use the corrected name, while a stopped task keeps the model it started with.
  3. To continue the stopped task instead, ask the person who runs the model service to bring back the model it was using, then select Resume. The stopped task can only continue with the model it started with.

What success looks like

  • Check saved model shows the correct model and passed, and the task gets an answer.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages your model service. Don't change your API key or turn off security checks; the problem is the model name or its access.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The model provider returned HTTP 400 or 404 with code model_not_found or deployment_not_found for the requested model or deployment identifier.

What this means

  • Chat routing rejected the requested identifier. A deployment alias can differ from a model family name, and a model list need not enumerate all valid aliases. This diagnosis comes from the rejected request, not absence from a listing.

Why this can happen

  • Chat routing rejected the requested identifier. A deployment alias can differ from a model family name, and a model list need not enumerate all valid aliases. This diagnosis comes from the rejected request, not absence from a listing.

How to diagnose it

  • The provider explicitly reported a missing model or deployment identifier.
  • A request using the intended identifier completes successfully.

How to fix it

  • Verify the exact served model id or cloud deployment name and the account's access to it (GET <base_url>/models lists served ids, though deployment aliases may not appear). Select the corrected name on the role card in Settings › Setup › Model routing for new tasks, or restore the original deployment so a saved task can resume with its captured model.
  • Verify the exact served model or cloud deployment identifier and account access. Select the corrected identifier for a new task, or restore the original deployment for a saved task.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded condition before trying the affected request again. Inspect existing operation receipts before resuming saved work.

How to verify the fix

  • A request using the intended identifier completes successfully.

What not to do

  • Do not replay completed work or weaken authentication and certificate checks to clear this diagnostic.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic describes the observed failure; it does not establish the outcome of earlier operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
